senses.gloss:
Lomaharṣaṇa
(‘one who raises the hair [of the listeners]’)
------------------------------------------
Lomaharṣaṇa (also spelt as रोमहर्षण) is a familiar figure that we come across in the पुराणस् as the chief narrator, especially to the ṛṣis engaged in a सत्त्रयाग and mostly in नैमिषारण्य, the Naimiṣa forest (identified with the modern Nimsar in Uttar Pradesh). He was also known as सूतपुराणिक. He was a disciple of वेदव्यास. His son was Ugraśravas who later on took his ड़थेर्’s place as the chief narrator of पुराणस्.
He had six disciples through whom the पुराणस् gradually took the present shape. They were: Sumati, Agnivarcas, Mitrāyus, Śāṁsapāyana, Akṛtavarṇa and Sāvarṇi.
